result.title: Perceptual Weight Space Programming for Diffusion Super-Resolution
result.summary: Diffusion models for image super-resolution can recover scene content while producing distracting artifacts or unbalanced colors. We study whether a large language model (LLM) can improve perceptual quality by editing a small subset of existing U-Net weights without a clean reference image. The proposed framework provides the editor with architecture code, selected weights, activation summaries, and sampling previews. It permits up to 1,020 candidate trials while limiting accepted changes to three layers and fewer than 0.1\% of model parameters. The evaluation protocol uses ResShift, SinSR, and SUPIR and compares GPT-6 Astra with a specified Qwen3-VL model under matched access. Feedback metrics guide editing, while separate quality metrics and blinded human comparisons evaluate the final weights. We also report an executed color calibration experiment using real photographs and two small residual networks. This experiment demonstrates correction of a fixed color shift and reveals that an improving feedback score can accompany worse performance on unseen scenes. A separate lightweight super-resolution experiment isolates modest changes in luminance detail while preserving color. The findings motivate restricted updates and independent evaluation of perceptual weight editing.

AI.brief_summary: 该工作让 LLM 依据架构代码、部分权重、激活摘要与采样预览，在无干净参考图条件下编辑扩散超分 U-Net 的少量权重，并比较不同模型作为编辑器与人工盲评的效果。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「反馈指标上升但未见场景变差」的观察与受限更新后独立评估的做法，可能为 latent 推理中代理奖励驱动的轨迹训练与泛化评价提供核查线索，但领域与推理期状态机制无关。
